name: InvestTable
subtitle: Compound interest calculator
promotionalText: See what a monthly deposit could grow to at a steady return, month by month. It is a projection, not a forecast, and you can try a loss as easily as a gain.
description:
InvestTable is a compound interest calculator. Type what you put in every month, the return you want to try and how many years to run it, and it shows the balance month by month, with every return reinvested.

It started as a spreadsheet I used for this, and it still does the math the same way.

What you set
• The amount you pay in every month
• The return, per month, per quarter or per year
• Dividends, as a yearly percentage of what you hold
• How many years to run it, from 1 to 30

What you get
• The balance at the end, how much of it you paid in and how much came from the returns
• A chart of the balance against what you paid in, on a linear or a log scale
• A month by month table for every year
• Count in rubles, dollars or euros, and convert the final balance between them at rates from open.er-api.com or ones you type in yourself

Returns can be negative too, so you can see what a bad stretch does to the same plan.

This is a projection, not a forecast. It assumes the same return every month, reinvested in full, and it counts no fees, taxes or inflation. Real returns vary and can be negative. The app names no funds, stocks or brokers, and nothing in it is investment advice.

Your figures stay on your device. There is no account and no sign-up, and it works offline. Without a connection the converter uses the last rates it fetched, or the ones built into the app.

20 languages, with numbers written the way your language writes them. Light, dark or automatic theme.

Privacy
Once a day the app sends anonymous usage counts: which features were used, the app version, platform, language and error counts. No IDs, none of your figures and nothing you type. The switch at the bottom of the page turns it off, and turning it off deletes the counts that were not sent yet. The privacy policy lists exactly what is sent.

Free, no ads.
reviewNotes:
InvestTable is an offline compound interest calculator. The user types every figure. The app names no securities, funds or brokers, gives no advice, sells nothing and has no accounts or sign-in. Everything is on one page: the projection at the top, the inputs under Your plan, then the chart, the month by month table and a currency converter. The theme, the language and the usage statistics switch are at the bottom of the page.

It makes two network calls: daily exchange rates from https://open.er-api.com, and one anonymous usage report a day to https://mrwd-metrics.vercel.app/api/ping (counts of features used, app version, platform, language and error counts, with no identifiers and none of the figures typed). The switch at the bottom of the page turns the report off. The app works fully without either call.

Guideline 5.1.1(ix) is about financial services from a legal entity. This is a calculator that the user feeds with their own numbers, so it should not apply. The exchange rates are shown with the credit the provider's free terms require.
